'''Catherine Bréchignac''' ({{IPA|fr|katʁin bʁeʃiɲak|-|Fr-Catherine Bréchignac.ogg}}; born 12 June 1946) is a [[French people|French]] [[physicist]]. She is a commander of the [[Légion d'honneur]], "secrétaire perpétuel honoraire" of the [[French Academy of Sciences|Académie des sciences]] and former president of the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]] ("National Centre for Scientific Research").<ref>{{cite web
  | last = Terraso
  | first = David
  | authorlink = 
  | title = Professor named president of Europe's largest scientific body
  | publisher = [[Georgia Institute of Technology]]
  | date = 2006-02-13
  | url = http://www.whistle.gatech.edu/archives/06/feb/13/brechignac.shtml
  | doi = 
  | accessdate = 2009-05-29
  | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110719201804/http://www.whistle.gatech.edu/archives/06/feb/13/brechignac.shtml
  | archive-date = 2011-07-19
  | url-status = dead
  }}</ref> ''[[The Times]]'' says she has "a formidable reputation for determination, decisiveness and an aptitude for analysing and clarifying complex matters."<ref name="Times">{{cite news 
  | last = 
  | first = 
  | title = At the centre of revolution in research: Catherine Bréchignac
  | work = [[Times Higher Education]]
  | place =
  | pages = 
  | language = 
  | publisher = 
  | date = 2000-04-14
  | url = http://www.timeshighereducation.co.uk/story.asp?storyCode=151148&sectioncode=26
  | accessdate = 2009-05-29}}</ref> As a president of the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]], she was responsible for 25,000 employees, 12,000 of whom are researchers, and a budget of 2.42 billion [[euro (currency)|Euros]].<ref name="Times" />

==Biography==
Daughter of the physicist [[Jean Teillac]], Catherine Bréchignac entered the [[École Normale Supérieure de Fontenay-aux-Roses]] in 1967, she received her ''DEA'' (Masters-level qualification) at the ''[[Faculté des sciences d'Orsay]]'' in 1971, her doctorate in 1977, and became a Research Director in 1985. In 1989, she became director of the Aimé Cotton laboratory and was Director General of the CNRS from 1997 to 2000. She clashed with [[Claude Allègre]], the minister at the time, over reforms she oversaw at the institution.<ref>{{cite web
  | last = 
  | first = 
  | authorlink = 
  | title = Catherine Bréchignac
  | work = [[Les Échos (France)|Les Échos]]
  | publisher = 
  | language = French
  | date = 2008-06-18
  | url = http://www.lesechos.fr/info/analyses/4742376.htm
  | archive-url = https://archive.today/20120905203555/http://www.lesechos.fr/info/analyses/4742376.htm
  | url-status = dead
  | archive-date = 2012-09-05
  | doi = 
  | accessdate = 2009-05-29
  }}</ref> She became President of the ''Institut d'optique théorique et appliquée'' ("Institute of Optical Theory and Practice") in 2003 and of the ''Palais de la découverte'' ("Palace of Discovery") in 2004. In 2005, she was elected future president of the [[International Council for Science]] (ICSU).<ref name="ICSU">{{cite web
  | last = 
  | first = 
  | authorlink = 
  | title = Executive Board - ICSU President: Catherine Bréchignac
  | publisher = [[International Council for Science]]
  | date = 2009-06-02
  | url = http://www.icsu.org/5_abouticsu/STRUCT_ExeBoa_bios.html
  | doi = 
  | accessdate = 2009-05-29
  | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20090615145725/http://www.icsu.org/5_abouticsu/STRUCT_ExeBoa_bios.html
  | archive-date = 2009-06-15
  | url-status = dead
  }} ICSU]</ref> She was appointed President of the CNRS at the Council of Ministers of 11 January 2006 on the recommendation of [[François Goulard]], the [[Ministry of Higher Education and Research|minister for higher education and research]].<ref>{{cite news 
  | last = 
  | first = 
  | title = New president pledges to put science back at the top of CNRS agenda
  | work = [[Times Higher Education]]
  | place =
  | pages = 
  | language = 
  | publisher = 
  | date = 2006-02-09
  | url = http://www.timeshighereducation.co.uk/story.asp?storyCode=201327&sectioncode=26
  | accessdate = 2009-05-29}}</ref><ref>{{cite web
  | last = Blandin
  | first = Noël
  | authorlink = 
  | title = Catherine Bréchignac est nommée présidente du CNRS
  | work = République des Lettres
  | publisher = 
  | language = French
  | date =2006-01-12
  | url = http://www.republique-des-lettres.fr/1110-catherine-brechignac.php
  | format = 
  | doi = 
  | accessdate =2009-05-29}}</ref> She was replaced by [[Alain Fuchs]] in 2010, even though she was a candidate to her own succession.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.lemonde.fr/societe/article/2010/01/14/un-nouveau-patron-pour-le-cnrs_1291882_3224.html|title=Un nouveau patron à la tête du CNRS|journal=[[Le Monde]]|date=14 January 2010|last=Jacqué|first=Philippe|language=fr}}</ref> She was "secrétaire perpétuel" (permanent secretary) of the Académie des sciences, Division 1,<ref>{{Citation|url=http://www.academie-sciences.fr/en/About-us/contact-us.html|title = Contact us|publisher=Académie des sciences|accessdate=9 November 2015}}</ref> from 2011 to 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Communiques-de-presse/communique-de-presse-etienne-ghys-elu-secretaire-perpetuel-de-l-academie-des-sciences.html|lang=fr|title=Communiqué de presse : Étienne Ghys élu Secrétaire perpétuel de l'Académie des sciences|publisher=Académie des sciences|date=19 July 2018|accessdate=4 February 2019}}</ref>

==Field==
According to the International Council for Science, Bréchignac co-founded the field of [[Cluster (physics)|cluster physics]], which straddles the gap between atomic, molecular and solid-state physics.<ref name="ICSU" /> Clusters are "the precursors of nano-objects."<ref name="ICSU" />

{{col-begin}}{{col-2}}
* President of the CNRS
* Member of the Institute

{{col-2}}
* [[CNRS Silver Medal]] (1994)
* Correspondent member of the [[French Academy of Sciences|Academy of Sciences]] (1997)
* Winner of the [[Fernand Holweck Medal and Prize|Holweck Medal]] (2003)
* Member of the Academy of Sciences (2005)
* [[Doctor Honoris Causa]] of the [[Freie Universität Berlin]] (2003), the [[Georgia Tech]] Institute (2006) and the [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]] (2007)<ref name="ICSU" />
* Member of [[Academia Europaea]] (2009)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Brechignac_Catherine|title=Catherine Bréchignac|work=Members|publisher=Academia Europaea|access-date=2026-10-01}}</ref>
